CausalChain: Tumor cells -> secrete EVs enriched in specific miRNAs -> uptake of EVs by mature myeloid cells -> suppression of IRF-8 and C/EBPα expression -> aberrant differentiation of myeloid cells into MDSCs -> accumulation of immunosuppressive MDSCs -> enhanced T cell inhibition and tumor immune escape
Hypothesis: Tumor-derived extracellular vesicles carry specific microRNAs that downregulate key myeloid differentiation factors (e.g., IRF-8, C/EBPα), thereby converting mature myeloid cells into immunosuppressive MDSCs; targeting this EV-miRNA axis may restore proper myeloid differentiation and enhance the efficacy of cancer immunotherapies.
Abstract: Recent insights into cancer immunotherapy have highlighted the central role of myeloid‐derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) in evading T cell‐mediated anti-tumor responses. Although numerous studies have detailed the cytokine and chemokine networks driving MDSCs expansion, emerging evidence suggests that tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) may actively reprogram mature myeloid cells into potent immunosuppressive MDSCs. Here, we propose a novel framework in which EVs, enriched with specific microRNAs, target essential transcription factors responsible for proper myeloid differentiation, such as IRF-8 and C/EBPα. This EV-mediated downregulation disrupts myelopoiesis, leading to the accumulation of MDSCs that enhance tumor immune evasion and resistance to checkpoint inhibitors. By inhibiting EV release or the activity of these microRNAs, it may be possible to restore normal myeloid differentiation and improve the efficacy of current immunotherapies.
